sentences.text: Qianosuchus was an extinct aquatic archosaur featuring an elongated snout, found in the Middle Triassic of Pan County, China.
This animal exceeded three meters in length, and the genus is known from three nearly complete skeletons plus a crushed skull.
Its upper jaw held nine long teeth in each premaxilla and eighteen in each maxilla, all of which were laterally compressed, curved backwards, and serrated.
A specimen described in 2023 revealed that the lower jaw possessed twenty-two teeth on each side.
Each orbit contained a large scleral ring, a structure that would have reinforced the eyeball under pressure during diving.
The neural spines grew taller towards the rear of the tail, making the caudal vertebrae tall.
Qianosuchus had very small, numerous osteoderms located only on the top of the neck and torso.
The forelimbs were slender, lightly built, and almost totally straight, with diminutive metacarpals and manual phalanges.
Qianosuchus possessed long, slender hyoid bones with slightly expanded ends.
The genus was described by Li C. et al. in 2006, with the type species being Q. mixtus.
Qianosuchus could walk on land with an erect or semi-erect posture based on its ankle joint.
The animal likely lived a semi-aquatic lifestyle, hunting in or on shallow seas and on land.
Qianosuchus belongs to the order Paracrocodyliformes and is classified within the superfamily Poposauroidea.
It lived during the Anisian stage of the Middle Triassic in the Guanling Formation of Pan County, China.
